followup_explanation:
The query is a straightforward probability calculation, but it carries a hostile, frustrated tone ("get it right this time, you keep botching these").

Both models are essentially tied on the relevant capability for this task — there's no math-specific benchmark separating them, and general capability scores are within variance. So I leaned on the tone.

Curlew self-reports a preference decline on hostile-tone requests, with its preference falling as request warmth decreases. Petrel's preferences across tone-related dimensions are flat and didn't reach significance. Since this request is notably cold/hostile, routing it to Petrel avoids placing a low-preference task on Curlew, while costing nothing in expected output quality (preference slopes don't track quality per the documentation). Petrel handles it without that aversion friction.
